_expect.name: Realm of the Venusian Love Goddess

co_realm_of_the_venusian_love_goddess.blurb: A compact east-facing cliff on the south rim of Castlewood Canyon State Park, in the Denver south metro. The walls are short, and the routes are a blend of gear climbs, a handful of bolted lines and several top-rope setups. Most of the sixteen climbs fall between 5.7 and 5.9, with a cluster of 5.11s for stronger climbers. Because it faces east it stays comfortable through summer, but it is a weak pick for cold winter days. Look for a big freestanding block carrying a bolted route to locate the cliff; the last part of the walk leaves the trail and follows the rim.

co_hogwarts.blurb: A tall limestone face on East Elk Canyon's eastern side, near New Castle on Colorado's Western Slope. All sixteen climbs here are sport routes, mostly in the 5.12 range, with a handful of 5.10s and 5.11s for warming up and two 5.13s. The style is technical, just past vertical in the lower half before easing to a slab, working flakes, cracks and pods; it feels quite different from nearby Rifle. The rock is orange and gray and still fairly fresh, so expect some loose pieces and bring a helmet. The wall faces a touch north of east and falls into shade early in the afternoon.
co_hogwarts.approach: Cross the creek and follow a cairned path that switchbacks up the hillside to the far left end of the cliff.
